input: Set up a side income tracker in a spreadsheet

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The number and type of income streams (freelance, reselling, rentals, investments, etc.) determines how many columns, categories, and sheets are needed.
Whether this is for personal use only or shared with a partner, accountant, or client changes the level of detail, labelling, and access permissions required.
The tool used (Google Sheets, Excel, Notion, Airtable, etc.) determines what formulas, features, and sharing options are available.
Knowing whether tax reporting is a hard requirement shapes whether fields like tax category, deductible expenses, and net profit must be included.
How often the user will log entries (daily, weekly, per transaction) affects whether the design should optimise for quick data entry or periodic batch updates.
Whether the user wants a minimal log vs. a dashboard with charts and summaries changes the complexity and visual design of the spreadsheet significantly.
Knowing the primary output the user cares about most (monthly totals, year-over-year trends, per-client breakdowns, etc.) determines what summary views and calculations to prioritise.

gold.taskTitle: Build a Side Income Tracker Spreadsheet
gold.taskDescription: Set up a spreadsheet to track income earned from one or more side activities, covering what gets recorded, how it is organised, and what insights it should surface.

questions.title: Which side income sources do you need to track?
questions.description: Identify the specific income streams (e.g., freelance writing, Etsy shop, Uber, rental property) so the tracker covers the right categories and fields.

questions.title: Who else will use or view this spreadsheet?
questions.description: Determine if this is solely for personal use or if a partner, accountant, or tax preparer also needs access, which affects structure and labelling.

questions.title: Which tool will you build this in?
questions.description: Confirm the platform — Google Sheets, Microsoft Excel, Notion, Airtable, or another — since available formulas and features differ widely.

questions.title: Does this need to support tax reporting or expense deductions?
questions.description: Establish whether tax categories, deductible expenses, or net profit calculations are required hard constraints, not just nice-to-haves.

questions.title: How often will you log new income entries?
questions.description: Understand the update cadence — per transaction, weekly, or monthly — to design the entry layout for minimum friction at that frequency.

questions.title: Do you want a simple log or a visual dashboard with charts?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user prefers a clean, minimal data table or a richer view with graphs, colour coding, and automated summaries.

questions.title: What is the one number or view you most want to see at a glance?
questions.description: Pinpoint the primary output — monthly total, income by source, profit after expenses, etc. — to ensure the tracker is built around that priority.
